page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance within the N2D family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. The machine supplies 16 virtual CPUs allocated across 8 physical cores via 2 threads per core, backed by dedicated vCPU allocation. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB total, delivering a lean 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, along with standard AVX extensions. The instance includes no local storage and operates with zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results show solid single-core performance alongside dependable multi-core throughput. Stress-ng single-core compute performance ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2,693.38, while stress-ng multi-core testing lands in the middle tier at 21,558.27. Geekbench results record a single-core score of 1,476.0 and a multi-core score of 9,379.0, supplemented by a 13,457.0 score in Clang software compilation. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 75.4 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 40.36 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2,344.07 and an overall PassMark CPU score of 22,027.2.

Operating with a strict 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n2d-highcpu-16 instance is designed for cost efficiency in CPU-bound tasks where extra RAM would otherwise sit idle. Tradeoffs stem directly from its lean resource provisioning: with only 16 GB of system RAM across 16 vCPUs and no bundled local storage disks, memory-dense workloads and local I/O intensive databases are constrained. The instance is primarily suited for batch compute processing, CI/CD code compilation, high-throughput static web serving (benchmarked at 15.62 GB/sec), and distributed microservices where memory consumption per thread remains low.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and dedicated CPU allocation. The instance features 16.0 GB of memory, equating to 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and contains no local disks or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core compute performance in the top 25% via stress-ng, supported by balanced multi-core metrics including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,379.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 22,027.2. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 75.4 GB/sec. Given its low memory footprint relative to execution threads, this server type delivers cost-effective processing for compute-heavy workloads such as code compilation, CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, and static web serving.
